newsitem.title: USA: Exide says competitor protests contract.
newsitem.headline: Exide says competitor protests contract.

text.p: Exide Electronics Group Inc said on Friday that a competitor has filed a protest with the U.S. General Accounting Office (GAO) over a contract it received from the U.S. Air Force.
Exide said it does not know the basis of the complaint and decisions on bid protests are made by the GAO within three months after the protest.
The contract is for providing uninterruptible power systems, spare parts, systems integration, training, installation and maintenance, Exide said.
The contract has a base term of three years and a two-year renewal option, Exide said.

The contract is projected to be worth $375 million for the first three years and the two optional years are estimated to be worth $125 million each year, Karin Cram, corporate communications manager, said.
The name of the competitor was not immediately available.
